prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: Furthermore, no distinction shall be made on the basis of the political, jurisdictional or international status of the country or territory to which a person belongs, whether it be independent, trust, non-self-governing or under any other limitation of sovereignty.
DEMAND: no distinction shall be made on the basis of the political, jurisdictional or international status of the country or territory to which a person belongs
BEARER: a distinction

cli.result:
1. No distinction may be made on the basis of any one of these statuses (political, jurisdictional or international) of the country or territory a person belongs to. A distinction based on any single one of them, whether it concerns the person's country or their territory, is forbidden.
2. No distinction may be made on the basis of the overall status of the person's country or territory, meaning that status taken as a whole across its political, jurisdictional and international sides. On this reading, only a distinction based on that combined status is forbidden.

answer:
